chunks: Abu al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Tabari narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Karrash narrated to us, saying: My master Anas narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The remembrance of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, in the morning and in the evening is better than the striking of swords in the cause of Allah, Exalted and Mighty.

It means: Whoever remembers Allah in the morning, and remembers what was from him during the night of bad deeds, and seeks forgiveness of Allah and repents to Him, then when he goes out seeking what Allah has allotted for him, he goes out with his misdeeds removed and his sins forgiven.

And when he remembers Allah in the evening (which is the late afternoon), he reviews himself regarding what was from him during that day of extravagance against himself and neglect of his Lord's command; so when he remembers Allah, seeks forgiveness of Allah, and turns back [to Him], he returns to his family with his sins for that day forgiven.
And the testimony [of faith] is also praised only if it is from one who repents to Allah, seeking forgiveness for the disobedience of Allah, Exalted and Mighty.

key_terms.حطم السيوف: Striking of swords (metaphor for physical jihad)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of morning and evening remembrance of God compared to jihad?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq places this narration in the 'Chapter of Rare Meanings' to highlight the spiritual efficacy of consistent dhikh paired with introspection (muhasabah) over physical combat, framing it as a mechanism for daily spiritual purification. The text explicitly links the acceptance of martyrdom to the state of the repentant believer, suggesting that the merit of jihad is contingent upon sincere tawbah and the removal of minor sins through this daily routine.

en.basel-kadem: 99.	We were told by Abu’l-Hasan, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Ahmad al-Tabari, that he said: We were told by Abu Sa’eed, that he said: We were told by Khirash, that he said: We were told by my master, Anas, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family,

went out to his companions and said: The one who assures two things for me, I will assure to him Paradise. Abu Huraira then said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah. I will assure them to you. What are they? He said: The one who assures to me that which is between his jawbones and that which is between his legs, I will assure Paradise to him. It means the one who assures (the preservation of) his tongue and genital. The causes of misfortunes open from these two parts. The offense of the tongue is disbelief in Allah, false saying, calumny and faithlessness with regards to the Names of Allah and His Attributes, backbiting, gossip and accusation. That is among the offenses of the tongue. The offense of the genital is intercourse when it is not permitted by marriage nor possession with the right hand. Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: «And those who are, to their genitals, preserving, except upon their wives or what their right hands possess; (in that) they are, indeed, not to be blamed. Hence, the one who seeks beyond that, those are the transgressors.» (70:30-31)
